set.body:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md.

Goal (owner, 2026-09-18): "the best automatic recall-to-video mapper in the world; Sherlock and
FilmFestival are test cases (also Friends)." "Best": on a benchmark someone else can rerun, per
input track, on the cleanest test data available, the mapper beats language-model baselines, the
published Sherlock method and simple retrieval, read against a human ceiling; claimable only per
track, only against the baselines actually run, only on these corpora.

Structure: Phase 0 -> Phase 1a (sealed Friends split, fail-closed scorer, baselines incl. a local
pinned LLM) -> owner checkpoint -> Phase 1b (benchmark v1) and Phase 2 (mapper in the library,
priority 1; film-compiler slices, priority 2) -> Phase 3 (development climb H1-H5, then one final
test opening on Friends and Memento) -> Phase 4 (ship 1.0).

Recorded rulings govern by default: A (no research gate on engineering), C (all D1A slices), D (one
bundle per model; proposal text outside the bundle), E (1.0 waits for D1A-types, D1A-film and all of
D1B). P1 is undecided and nothing here assumes it.

Conventions: children are linked by `rel`; blocking order by `dep`; priority encodes the plan's
sequencing (0 = Phase 0/1a now, 1 = mapper slices, 1b, Phase 3/4, 2 = film-compiler slices,
3 = 1.x). Every gold read is ledgered before it happens.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Every child ticket is closed with its acceptance criteria met, or closed as superseded/rejected
   with a note saying why.
2. The Phase 4 release-gate ticket is closed (shipping gate).
3. The final test readout is committed (superiority-claim gate, separate from shipping).

Size: multi-month.
set.title: EPIC: best automatic recall-to-video mapper (plan 2026-09-18, revision 6)
